title: Applying Network Flow Analysis to Multi-Agent Communication Graphs for Anomaly Detection

original_idea.body:
# Applying Network Flow Analysis to Multi-Agent Communication Graphs for Anomaly Detection

**Problem:** Network flow analysis identifies anomalous traffic patterns (unusual volumes, new destinations, timing anomalies). The same principles could be applied to agent-to-agent communication flows.

**Direction:** Instrument a multi-agent system to log all inter-agent message flows (source, destination, message length, timestamp). Inject coordinated attack scenarios. Apply flow anomaly detection techniques (similar to NetFlow analysis) to identify attack sessions.

**Why it matters:** Flow-level analysis is computationally cheap and does not require examining message content — useful when messages are encrypted or in complex formats.

**Relevant context:** NetFlow network analysis; inter-agent collusion detection; multi-agent monitoring.
